<cite ref="Onkelos Genesis 11:31">Targ. Gen. XI, 31</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Gittin 57a:6">Gitt. 57ᵃ</cite> <he>כי הוו מפקי חתנא וכ׳</he> when they led forth bride and groom in procession.

<cite ref="Meilah 19a:22">Meïl. 19ᵃ</cite> <he>דהבא דכלתיה דנון</he> the gold ware of the daughter-in-law of Nun (which was found to have lost in weight); a. fr.—[<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 15:32">Targ. Job XV, 32</cite> <he>וכַלְתַיה</he>, v. <cite ref="K00557"><he>כִּילְתָא</he> I</cite>.]—Pl. <cite ref="K00784"><he>כַּלָּתָא</he></cite>, <he>כַּלָּתָה</he>, <cite ref="K00769"><he>כַּלָּן</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Ruth 1:6">Targ. Ruth I, 6</cite>.

<cite ref="Targum Jonathan on Jeremiah 7:34">Targ. Jer. VII, 34</cite>.—Meïl. l. c. <he>דהבא דרמיין כַּלָּתָיךְ</he> the gold ware which thy daughters-in-law cast carelessly about (by which they wear off).
<cite ref="Ketubot 17a:2">Keth. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>משרי קמי כ׳</he> they sang before (the processions of) brides.

<cite ref="Yevamot 21b:4">Yeb. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>כלתה דבי …</he> the daughters-in-law of the house of … (where there were wives of his daughter’s sons and wives of his son’s sons).—V. <cite ref="K00729"><he>כַּלַּיָּיה</he></cite>, <cite ref="K00739"><he>כַּלִּין</he></cite>.
